chunks: From him, from Abu Abdillah al-Razi, from Abu al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, from Zur'ah ibn Muhammad, from Sama'ah ibn Mihran, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Do not sell the Mushaf (copies of the Quran), for selling it is forbidden.' I asked: 'What do you say about buying it?' He said: 'Buy the two covers, the iron, and the binding, and beware of buying the paper upon which the Quran is written, for it becomes forbidden upon you and upon the one who sells it.'

key_terms.ٱلْمَصَاحِفَ: The copies of the Quran (plural of Mus'haf)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on selling physical copies of the Quran in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Sahih al-Tusi clarifies the juristic distinction between selling the Quran as a commodity versus purchasing the physical materials of the Mushaf. Scholars interpret the prohibition as applying to the text itself being treated as a tradeable good, whereas buying the paper, binding, and covers separately avoids this sanctity-based restriction. This ruling underscores the reverence for the Quranic text in Shia fiqh, ensuring it is not commodified in the same manner as ordinary goods.
